neutral_facts.value: The accused, a government official, was involved in a case of corruption. The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) registered a case against him for demanding a bribe. During the investigation, the accused and another individual were caught accepting a bribe. The CBI sought pardon for the second individual to assist in the investigation. The Metropolitan Magistrate granted pardon to the second individual, which was later challenged. The case was framed against the accused, and he was examined as a witness. The Special Judge rejected the challenge to the pardon, and the High Court dismissed the appeal. The Supreme Court held that the Metropolitan Magistrate had the power to grant pardon during the investigation, and the order was not a curable irregularity.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that during investigation, both the Special Judge and the Magistrate acting under Section 306 Cr.P.C. have concurrent jurisdiction to grant pardon, and that an order passed in good faith is a curable irregularity.

quotes.text: During investigation, both the Special Judge as well as the Magistrate acting u/s 306 Cr.P.C. have concurrent jurisdiction to entertain application of pardon, which facilitates proper investigation of the crime. But, after the committal of the case, the pardon granted by the Magistrate is not a curable irregularity.
